subject: Linguistics
title: Writing Direction
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Writing Direction.

hook.text: English goes left to right. Arabic goes right to left. Ancient Greek went both ways—alternating each line.

buildup.text: Writing direction isn't natural—it's a convention that varies across scripts.

discovery.text: Boustrophedon ('as the ox plows') reversed direction each line—some ancient scripts did this.

twist.text: Mongolian traditional script runs top to bottom in vertical columns—from left to right.

climax.text: Direction affects page layout, book binding, UI design, and even how readers scan images.

punchline.text: Which way you read shapes how you see the page.

quiz.question: What is boustrophedon?
options: Writing that reverses direction each line
